concepts.heading: Why Money Kills Relationships
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting back to back with a pile of bills between them
concepts.plain: Money causes more fights between partners than anything else.

concepts.heading: The Emotional Weight of Money
concepts.alt: A guide holding a coin that casts a heart-shaped shadow
concepts.plain: Money is never just about money. It carries feelings.

concepts.heading: Money Scripts
concepts.alt: A guide reading four small scrolls
concepts.plain: We all carry hidden beliefs about money. Researchers found four common ones.

concepts.heading: Money in Different Kinds of Relationships
concepts.plain: Money questions look different when you are dating, partnered or have several partners.

concepts.heading: The Cost of Financial Secrecy
concepts.alt: A guide hiding a shopping bag behind his back
concepts.plain: Many people hide money matters from a partner, and it breaks trust.

checks.prompt: What is the number one source of conflict in romantic relationships?
checks.explanation: Money. Money is the number one source of conflict in romantic relationships — more than sex, parenting, or household responsibilities.

checks.prompt: In one survey, what share of adults with combined finances admitted to financial deception?
checks.explanation: 43%. A National Endowment for Financial Education survey found that 43% of adults with combined finances admitted to financial deception — hiding purchases, accounts, debt, or income.

13397c18-28f7-4710-b1cc-c769c55aac6e.takeaway: Money fights are really about safety, freedom and trust. Secrets about money damage relationships.

concepts.heading: Financial Communication Skills
concepts.alt: A guide holding a calculator in one hand and a heart in the other
concepts.plain: Talking about money well is a skill most of us were never taught.

concepts.heading: Why Money Conversations Are So Hard
concepts.alt: A guide peeking out from behind a very large coin
concepts.plain: Shame makes money hard to talk about.

concepts.heading: The Money Date Framework
concepts.alt: At a cafe table with coffee, a notebook and a small piggy bank
concepts.plain: Plan regular "money dates": calm talks about money when nothing is on fire.

concepts.heading: Communication Techniques
concepts.alt: A guide speaking with a hand on her chest, an empty speech bubble with a small heart
concepts.plain: Say how you feel instead of accusing.

concepts.heading: Money Talks in Different Relationships
concepts.plain: Fit the money talk to the relationship.

concepts.heading: Building Financial Communication Muscles
concepts.alt: A guide lifting a small dumbbell whose weights are coins
concepts.plain: It gets easier the more you practise.

options: A regular, dedicated conversation about finances in a non-crisis context
checks.explanation: A regular, dedicated conversation about finances in a non-crisis context. Schedule regular "money dates" — dedicated conversations about finances in a neutral, non-crisis context.

checks.prompt: Which communication technique does the lesson recommend?
checks.explanation: "I" statements about feelings. Use "I" statements about feelings, not accusations about behaviour.

f5bdcc87-d20e-41e3-bde8-549e294ee628.takeaway: Schedule calm "money dates" and talk about feelings, not blame.

concepts.heading: Shared Resource Models
concepts.alt: A guide looking at five different jars on a shelf
concepts.plain: There is no single right way to organise money together.

concepts.heading: Model 1: Fully Merged Finances
concepts.alt: Two guides pouring coins together into one big shared pot
concepts.plain: Fully merged: everything goes into one shared pot.

concepts.heading: Model 2: Proportional Contribution
concepts.alt: A guide holding a balance scale with a large coin stack on one side and a small one on the other
concepts.plain: Proportional: each person pays a share based on what they earn.

concepts.heading: Model 3: The Three-Pot System
concepts.alt: A guide standing behind three jars of different colours
concepts.plain: Three pots: yours, mine and ours.

concepts.heading: Model 4: Complete Financial Independence
concepts.alt: Each happily holding their own separate piggy bank
concepts.plain: Fully separate: each person keeps their own money.

concepts.heading: Model 5: Polycule Financial Structures
concepts.plain: Groups of partners often mix these models.

concepts.heading: Choosing Your Model
concepts.plain: Think about things like how long you have been together.

concepts.heading: Practical Tools
concepts.alt: A guide using a phone that shows a colourful pie chart
concepts.plain: Budgeting apps and shared accounts help you see things without merging everything.

checks.prompt: In the proportional model, partners contribute…
checks.explanation: Based on income. Each partner contributes to shared expenses proportionally based on income.

options: Individual accounts plus a shared account
checks.explanation: Individual accounts plus a shared account. Each partner maintains individual accounts plus a shared account for joint expenses.

88e11642-b3fd-4e77-9e44-409638bd2876.takeaway: There are several fair ways to share money. Pick the one that fits your situation.

concepts.heading: Financial Boundaries & Partnership Building
concepts.alt: Each holding their own wallet while carrying one shared basket between them
concepts.plain: A healthy money relationship needs teamwork and independence.

concepts.heading: Financial Abuse: The Hidden Form of Control
concepts.alt: A guide looking at a wallet locked inside a small cage
concepts.plain: Controlling someone's money is abuse. It happens in almost all abusive relationships.

concepts.heading: Healthy Financial Boundaries
concepts.alt: A guide holding a key and an open ledger book
concepts.plain: You have the right to know about all shared money.

concepts.heading: Protecting Yourself Financially
concepts.alt: A guide holding her own bank card and a small shield
concepts.plain: Even in a good relationship, keep your own account and good credit.

concepts.heading: Income Inequality & Power
concepts.alt: Balanced level on a seesaw, each holding a different-sized bag of coins
concepts.plain: When one of you earns much more, watch that it does not turn into more say.

concepts.heading: Creating a Shared Financial Vision
concepts.alt: Each writing on their own page, then turning the pages toward each other
concepts.plain: Each write down your answers separately, then share them.

concepts.heading: Building Your Financial System Together
concepts.alt: At a table with a wall calendar, a notebook and tea
concepts.plain: Have a money talk every month.

concepts.heading: Navigating Financial Life Events
concepts.plain: Plan ahead for big changes, like moving in together or losing a job.

concepts.heading: Financial Resources for Couples
concepts.plain: Financial therapists and fee-only planners can help.

checks.after: Financial Abuse: The Hidden Form of Control
checks.prompt: In about what share of domestic violence cases does financial abuse occur?
checks.explanation: 99%. Financial abuse occurs in an estimated 99% of domestic violence cases (National Network to End Domestic Violence).

checks.prompt: Even in a healthy relationship, you should…
checks.explanation: Maintain your own bank account. Even in healthy relationships, maintain your own bank account and keep your credit in good standing.

b50abbe1-af1f-4d4c-a337-6740f31fb3b0.takeaway: You have a right to know about and access shared money. Keep some independence and plan together.
